title: A British agent at Port Sainte-Marie to the Duke of Newcastle, coded report c. July 1729 (Huntington mssBLA 191 p. 5)

documents.shelfmark: Huntington Library, William Blathwayt papers addenda, mssBLA 191, p. 5 (HDL p15150coll7 id 61005)
documents.route: El Puerto de Santa María -> London

plaintext.source: No gloss on the leaf; the same code is glossed interlinearly on sibling letters in mssBLA 187-191.

transcription.notes: 13 lines; one group at the end of line 1 overwritten (386); 702 on line 7 has a blot.

system.summary: One-part French numerical code, groups 1-1370, in alphabetical order: letters, syllables, words and names in one sorted list; groups from 1240 up act as separators.
system.sibling_key: Glossed sibling letters in mssBLA 187-191 (23 June, 29 June, 14 July 1729 and later) in the same code; the table was rebuilt from them.
system.notes: Same agent and code as the letter of 29 June 1729 that asks for a new cipher.

prior_solution.where: Huntington catalogue: 'in cipher', no decipherment; leaf unglossed (checked 28 Oct 2026). Not on DECODE.

conditions.human_role: Posed the target from the catalogue with /goal, pointing to the glossed siblings.

solution.what: Downloaded the 39 page images of mssBLA 191, 187, 188 and the 14 July and 4 Aug 1729 items from HDL IIIF.
Transcribed p. 5 (141 groups, 13 lines) into ct_p5.txt.
Two subagents transcribed the glossed siblings (60887, 60907-60909, 60917-60920, 60963): 942 code/gloss pairs, 364 distinct codes.
Applied the sibling table to p. 5 (decode.py): 116 of 141 groups read directly; the decode forms French sentences.

Filled 18 groups from context bracketed by the alphabetical order of the code (585 ig in ig-no-re/ig-no-ra-n-ce, 275 dans, 222 conduite, 816 ordre, 1210 six between cinq and sept, 666 lu, 1118 trouver ...).
Read the decode as sentences and translated it; 134 of 141 groups read, 7 open (6, 274, 254, 937, 1052, 726, 836).

Strict recount while verifying the duplicate PR #448 (targets/newcastle1729, same document and key): of the 141 groups, 116 carry a value glossed in the sibling letters (decode.py on pairs_A.tsv and pairs_B.tsv); the 18 tokens filled from the sense and the alphabetical order (pairs_zinf.tsv) and the 7 unread are holes. Read share 0.823, class set to read in part, key partial. Group 1118: filled here as 'trouver', but mssBLA 194 (HDL 60893 l. 14, checked on the image, retouched ink) glosses it 'tain'; both recorded, group marked [?trouver / ?tain], neither adopted. The earlier 134 of 141 (0.95) is withdrawn. The two pairs files hold 1,055 glossed pairs (364 distinct codes), not the 942 first reported.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The code table was rebuilt from the interlinear decipherments on five sibling letters of the same agent in the same file and applied to the unglossed p. 5. Gaps filled from the sense and the code's alphabetical order were first counted as read; since 12 Nov 2026 they count as holes.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 116 of 141 groups of ct_p5.txt carry a value glossed in the sibling letters (decode.py with pairs_A.tsv and pairs_B.tsv; 12 Nov 2026 strict count). 18 further tokens (15 codes) filled from the sense and the alphabetical order (pairs_zinf.tsv) and 7 without a value are holes. The earlier figure, 134 of 141 (0.95), counted the 18 inferred tokens as read.

validation.notes: code table read off contemporary glosses, not recovered by search

outcome.notes: The agent complains that Keene leaves him without orders during the accommodation and asks Newcastle for instructions. Group 1118 is open: filled here as 'trouver' from the sense, but glossed 'tain' in mssBLA 194 (HDL 60893 l. 14, retouched ink), recorded in targets/newcastle1729/. targets/newcastle1729 is the same document and key (duplicate folder, in progress).

texts.label: mssBLA 191 p. 5, agent at Port Sainte-Marie to Newcastle, c. July 1729
texts.summary: The agent thanks 'Milord' for his letter, says he answered on the sixth at the first address, complains that Mr Keene (British envoy at Madrid) has given him no orders for weeks about the accommodation, and asks for orders for his conduct. Written during the negotiations that led to the Treaty of Seville (Nov 1729). Read in part: 116 of 141 groups carry a glossed value; the rest is filled from the sense or open.

reading_review.by: an AI agent, strict recount of 12 Nov 2026
reading_review.note: The decode reads as coherent French and the glossed words build most clauses, but 18 tokens are filled from the sense and 7 groups are open, so nearly every sentence carries a hole; read share 0.823 (class: read in part).

gaps.item: 18 tokens (15 codes) filled from the sense and the alphabetical order only: 805, 585 (2), 275 (2), 222, 816 (2), 666, 1118, 689, 460, 84, 1152, 1210, 285, 711, 1250
gaps.detail: No gloss in the sibling letters transcribed here. mssBLA 194 glosses 1118 as 'tain', in conflict with the value 'trouver' filled here. The duplicate folder newcastle1729 has glosses for 84 and 816 in other letters (not re-checked on the images) and for 275 and 666 by reading a digit differently or from a blotted group; none for the others.

Not glossed in any sibling here; alphabetical neighbours narrow each only to a letter range (274/254 d-, 937 qu-, 1052 s-, 726 m-, 836 p-); 6 is a number. newcastle1729 reads 60919 L11 as 937 = monsieur where this folder has 737; the digit is not settled on the image (12 Nov 2026), and 119 of 141 (0.844) would be valued if it and 275 are as newcastle1729 reads them.
